source_caption:
Rebecca Cammisa’s Which Way Home follows several unaccompanied children as they make the dangerous journey through Mexico, hoping to reach the United States.

Many of them travel on top of freight trains known as “The Beast,” risking serious injury as they move north. But the film isn’t simply about the journey itself. It stays close to the children, giving them space to explain why they left home, what they’re running from, and what they hope to find on the other side.

The documentary introduces children with very different stories. Some hope to reunite with family members already living in the U.S., while others are searching for better opportunities or a way to help their families back home. Along the way, they face exhaustion, detention, uncertainty and the constant dangers surrounding the migration route.

Cammisa spent years working on the film and traveled alongside migrants to document their experiences. Rather than focusing only on immigration as a political issue, Which Way Home makes the story personal by showing the journey through the eyes of children who are still trying to understand where their lives are headed.

The film premiered at the 2009 Tribeca Film Festival and was later shortlisted for the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature.

source_details.title: Which Way Home
source_details.synopsis: Which Way Home is a 2009 documentary film directed by Rebecca Cammisa that follows several children who are attempting to get from Mexico and Central America to the United States on top of a freight train that crosses Mexico known as "La Bestia" (The Beast). Cammisa received a Fulbright Scholar Grant to make the documentary in 2006. The film premiered on HBO on August 24, 2009.
